content:
According to toxicology reports obtained by multiple media outlets on Tuesday, actress Hayden Panettiere died from the toxic effects of fentanyl and several other substances.

The cause of death for the 36-year-old woman was ruled an accident by the Greenville County, South Carolina coroner's office, which conducted an autopsy after her death at an apartment in Greenville on August 16.

The report noted that the other substances contributing to her death and detected in her system also included 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol, and quetiapine.

The coroner's report stated: 'No trauma was observed at the time of autopsy that could have led to her demise.'

According to information from the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, 4-ANPP is a controlled substance commonly found in the illicit manufacturing process of fentanyl. Alprazolam, better known by its trade name 'Xanax', is used to treat anxiety and panic disorders. Methocarbamol is a prescription muscle relaxant, while quetiapine is prescribed to treat schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder.

The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration joined the investigation several days after her death alongside local and state officials, according to people familiar with the matter cited by ABC News at the time.

The star of "Heroes" and "Nashville" was found unresponsive with her on-again, off-again boyfriend Brian Hickerson and her brother Zach Hickerson present. According to a heavily redacted police report, paramedics performed "prolonged" resuscitation efforts before she was ultimately pronounced dead at the scene.

Panettiere's relationship with Brian Hickerson has long been characterized as volatile and unhealthy, with Hickerson having been arrested multiple times since 2019 on suspicion of domestic violence against her.

According to TMZ, the two brothers were not invited to attend Panettiere's memorial service held in Malibu, California, over the past weekend.
